omissions.reason: Natural Earth U.S. administrative subunits are not used for radio classification; detailed Census geometry supplies those fields, including separate Kure, Swains and Desecheo treatment.

No whole-feature DXCC correspondence is asserted. Unclassified records include multi-entity geography requiring additional splits (Canada, Greece, Brazil, Australia, Chile, Colombia, Fiji, Kiribati, Malaysia, Mauritius, New Caledonia, Cook Islands, French Polynesia, Russia, Taiwan), disputed/nonentity areas and remaining outlying islands. Geographic omission is preferable to asserting a whole ordinary administrative unit equals one radio entity; the maintained correspondence table identifies every supported selected subunit.

The entire pinned minor-islands source is omitted. All 2,795 selected minor-island records lack names, administrative identity or a unique publisher key: their attributes are only featurecla, min_zoom and scalerank. None receives an inferred entity from proximity; separate supported island subunits retain their explicit correspondence.

The original Natural Earth PCN feature contains four components: Pitcairn, Ducie, Henderson and Oeno. Ducie (near 124.79 W, 24.67 S) is separate DXCC entity 513, while Pitcairn is 172. No whole-feature value is supported without a reviewed component correspondence; this feature remains unclassified.
citations: Pinned Natural Earth 5.1.1 PCN original component inspection; source archive/semantic feature provenance retained in the resolved recipe and manifest.

omissions.reason: The original Natural Earth NZA feature includes the Snares component near 166.6 E, 48 S. ARRL's 2015 clarification places Auckland, Campbell, Antipodes and Bounty in entity 16 but specifically excludes the Snares. No whole-feature entity 16 assignment is supported without a reviewed component split; this feature remains unclassified.
citations: Pinned Natural Earth 5.1.1 NZA original component inspection; source archive/semantic feature provenance retained in the resolved recipe and manifest.

omissions.reason: The original Natural Earth CRI feature includes Cocos Island near 5.53 N, 87.07 W, far southwest of mainland Costa Rica. Cocos is separate DXCC entity 37; mainland Costa Rica is 308. No whole-feature value is supported without a reviewed component split; this feature remains unclassified.
citations: Pinned Natural Earth 5.1.1 CRI original component inspection; source archive/semantic feature provenance retained in the resolved recipe and manifest.

omissions.reason: The original Natural Earth ESX feature includes African Spanish island components, including a Chafarinas component near 35.18 N, 2.43 W. The official Islands On The Air AF-036 directory places Chafarinas in Ceuta and Melilla (DXCC 32), while mainland Spain is 281. Separate Natural Earth SEC and SEM records therefore do not establish a correct whole-feature ESX assignment. ESX remains unclassified without a reviewed component split.

scope: Selected Census U.S. states/territories and county equivalents, retaining eight actual Connecticut counties; explicit radio correspondence and worldwide omissions.
limitations: Census is not survey-grade boundary data.
HA8TKS zone linework has unestablished survey lineage and requires reviewed corrections.
Natural Earth is generalized cartography with incomplete small-island/polar coverage.

ITU zones 74 and 75 explicitly cover full-longitude bands from 80 to 85 degrees south/north. Their guarded interpretation preserves those exact extents; ITU coverage beyond 85 degrees remains unknown. Retaining all 90 source records does not infer polar caps.

Census administrative geometry includes waters, not only coastlines. Caribbean regional grid assignments use all selected land FACES within the published operation extent; residual waters use disclosed D259 no-shift. Exact mixed-operation seams remain measurable and are not silently snapped.
